lesson.menu_desc: Lessons 21-29 in one conversation, plus topic bridges (speaking of which, that reminds me) -- reading model -- 30 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 30 — Mid-Program Fluency Review
lesson.title_tag: Professor View — Vanessa Giuriati | Lesson 30 — Mid-Program Fluency Review

listenings.text: In a real conversation, topics do not wait for permission. They jump. Someone mentions a trip, and a minute later you are talking about their mother, and then about work. Native speakers move between topics with small phrases that act like bridges. Speaking of which connects the new topic to the last one. That reminds me says that something you just heard brought back a memory. By the way adds something small. And when you want to return to an earlier point, going back to what you said is perfect. Without these bridges, a change of topic sounds like a bump. With them, it sounds like a conversation. You do not need many. Three or four, used naturally, are enough to make you sound relaxed, even when you are not.

Somewhere around the middle of learning a language, almost everyone hits a plateau. At the beginning, progress is obvious. Every week you can say things you could not say before. Then, around the intermediate level, the progress becomes invisible. You are still improving, but you cannot feel it, and that is when many people give up. The trick is to measure differently. Do not ask whether you are fluent. Ask smaller questions. Did I speak for two minutes without stopping? Did I change topics without freezing? Did I disagree without apologizing? Record yourself once a month and listen to the old recordings. The difference you cannot feel from week to week is very easy to hear from month to month.

extra_audio.text: First, I listen to what the other person is talking about, for example a trip. Then I connect a new topic to it: speaking of which, how was your weekend? After that, something they say makes me remember a story: that reminds me of my first job. Next, I return to an earlier point: going back to what you said about work. In the end, I move to something completely new: on a different note, are you free on Friday?

paras: Thirty lessons ago, I could read a report in English without problems, but I could not say two sentences in a meeting without planning them in Portuguese first. My teacher asked me what I wanted, and I said, honestly, to stop being afraid of my own voice.

Some things changed faster than I expected. I used to apologize before every sentence. Now I start with "There's something I wanted to bring up", and people listen. Speaking of which, I have also stopped saying "I'm fine" when I'm not. That one surprised my husband more than my boss.

Other things are still hard. When a conversation jumps from one topic to another, I still freeze for a second. My teacher gave me a small toolkit for that: "that reminds me", "going back to what you said", "on a different note". Anyway, I am not fluent yet, and I have stopped pretending that I will be by December.

To sum up: I am not a different person. I am the same person, with more doors open. For the next ten lessons, I have three goals: to tell longer stories, to disagree without apologizing, and to change topics without freezing.
